Conjecture 2 is quite optimistic, as it implies the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture (see [3] and the citations therein) by setting ai=1a_{i}=1 for all i∈{1,…,n−1}i\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\} and an=0a_{n}=0. In fact, Conjecture 2 is also related to the stronger Aharoni-Berger conjecture (see [4]).
Remark 1. In light of Proposition 1.1, it is natural to ask how close to a fairly split perfect matching we can get for k≥3k\geq 3.

Remark 2. We note that the bound n−2n-2 in Theorem 1.2 cannot be improved for general graphs without extra assumptions. To see this, for any even n>2n>2 one can consider the (unique) decomposition of n/2n/2 disjoint copies of K4K_{4} into three perfect matchings M1,M2,M3M_{1},M_{2},M_{3}.
Conjecture 1.4 is easy to show when there are at most two non-zero colour-multiplicities.
